rationale: C07 plausibly supplied a material drafting template for the child. Both letters defend a major defense-construction program against congressional reductions by emphasizing that the program was carefully reviewed, reduced to the minimum essential facilities, and remained indispensable to national security. The close timing, shared recipient form, parallel argumentative sequence, and unusually similar minimum-essential formulation make C07 stronger than the flood-control letters, which share the House-cut and minimum-budget machinery but concern civil works and use a more extended argument.

shared_material.child_excerpt: We urgently need the air bases and depots and other installations... They are absolutely vital to our whole defense plan.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: this expansion program is integral to the necessary strengthening of our military defenses
shared_material.explanation: Both characterize a construction program as an indispensable component of the overall defense effort.

shared_material.child_excerpt: When this program was submitted to the Congress, it had already been pared down to the minimum that safety would allow.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The program has been carefully reviewed in order to bring its total cost down to a practicable minimum. Every effort has been made to exclude facilities not essential
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive shared drafting: prior review, reduction to a minimum, and exclusion of nonessential facilities are used to rebut further cuts.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The House Armed Services Committee considered the program with care and found that the items in the House Bill were thoroughly justified.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I recently have asked the members of the special committee... to reconsider it... This reconsideration... clearly verifies that this expansion program is integral
shared_material.explanation: Each invokes a committee's careful review and favorable conclusion as validation of the program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It would be a terrible disaster to lose half these facilities at a stroke.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: We must nevertheless continue our efforts to buttress the security of this country and of the free world. Not to do so invites disaster.
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude that withholding the requested defense facilities would risk disaster.
